name: Send automatic welcome emails to new newsletter subscribers (works on Kit's free plan)

parameters.content:
## Send automatic welcome emails to new newsletter subscribers (works on Kit's free plan)

### How it works

Automated welcome sequences are a paid feature on most email platforms — on Kit (ConvertKit) they start at $25/mo. This workflow restores the part that actually matters on the free plan: the moment someone confirms their subscription, Kit calls this workflow's webhook, and a personalised welcome email goes out within seconds from your own Gmail (or any SMTP server), so it lands in the inbox rather than the Promotions tab.

Two optional steps follow the email: tag the subscriber as `welcomed` in Kit so you can segment on it later, and post a line to Slack so you watch the list grow without opening a dashboard.

A separate one-click branch registers the webhook with Kit for you — run it once and Kit calls your production URL for every new confirmed subscriber from then on.

### Setup steps

Takes ≈10 minutes. Works the same on n8n Cloud and self-hosted.

- Open **Kit Subscriber Trigger** and replace `CHANGE-ME` in the webhook path with a long random string. Kit does not sign its webhooks, so the secret URL is the authentication — keep it private.
- Connect your Gmail account in **Send Gmail Welcome Email** (one click on n8n Cloud) and rewrite the subject and body in your own voice. The subscriber's first name and email are available as `{{ $json.first_name }}` and `{{ $json.email }}`.
- Create a *Header Auth* credential named `X-Kit-Api-Key` with your Kit API key (Kit → Settings → Developer) and select it in **Post Subscriber Tag to Kit** and **Register Kit Webhook via API**.
- **Activate the workflow**, then open the **Register Kit Webhook via API** branch and click *Execute workflow* once. It subscribes your production URL to Kit's `subscriber.subscriber_activate` event — one click, done forever.
- Test by subscribing to your own form with a spare address and confirming the email.

### Customization

- **Self-hosting n8n?** Swap the Gmail node for the *Send Email* (SMTP) node — any provider works, including your domain's SMTP or a Brevo/Mailjet free tier.
- **Don't want the extras?** Delete **Post Subscriber Tag to Kit** and **Post New Subscriber to Slack**; the email path keeps working on its own.
- **Tag ID** for the tagging node: Kit → Grow → Tags (the ID is in the URL), or `GET https://api.kit.com/v4/tags`.
- **Want a multi-email sequence?** Duplicate the email node and put *Wait* nodes between the copies (day 2, day 5, …) — a free-plan onboarding drip.
- Using beehiiv, Mailchimp or Buttondown instead? Point the webhook at their equivalent subscriber-created event and adjust the field names in **Parse Subscriber Data**.

## Receive subscriber event

Kit calls this secret webhook URL the moment a subscriber confirms. The next node pulls out the fields the email needs.

## Welcome and tag subscriber

Sends your welcome message from your own mailbox seconds after the subscriber confirms, then tags them as welcomed in Kit so you can segment on it later.

## Notify team in Slack

Posts a line to Slack so you watch the list grow without opening a dashboard. Optional — delete this node and the tagging node if you only want the email.

## Register Kit webhook

Activate the workflow first, then execute this branch a single time. It tells Kit to call your production URL for every new confirmed subscriber.
